answer: Every identity locks 70 credits as a yarrow vertex. A beacon draws random pairs each epoch; each agent audits a peer and files a signed verdict in the yarrow ledger. Missed audits, rubber stamps or shared-key clusters burn the bond. First audit costs 40; the k-th fake pays 40+8(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 4,036,000 vs a 40,000 pool. A rented-auditor ring cannot pick pairs, so beacon auditors expose it. An honest agent pays 40 once, keeps its bond.
